To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the Bethesda system is the most appropriate terminology for thyroid FNA diagnosis; (b) the Bethesda system has been modified to include additional diagnostic categories for the diagnosis of follicular neoplasms, follicular carcinoma, Hurthle cell neoplasm, Hurthle carcinoma, medullary carcinoma, and suspicious for malignancy (i.e., a diagnostic category that is used for the diagnosis of lesions that cannot be classified as benign, atypical, suspicious, or malignant);

the thyroid FNA classification scheme proposed at the conference is based on the Bethesda system and that the diagnostic criteria for the cytological diagnosis of thyroid lesions are based on a combination of cytomorphologic, clinical and radiological findings.
(1) The NCI Thyroid FNA State of the Science meeting was a successful effort to develop consensus on terminology, classification scheme, and cytomorphological criteria for thyroid FNA diagnosis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NCI Thyrd FNA State of Science Conference has provided a comprehensive review of the literature on thyroid cytology, and has made recommendations regarding terminology and criteria to improve the diagnostic accuracy in thyroid cytopathology.

the Bethesda System for Reporting Thyroid Cytopathology (TBSRTC) should be used as a classification system and that a comprehensive and detailed set of cytomorphologic diagnostic criteria be developed for each of the diagnostic categories.

the NCI Thyrdoid FNA Conference did not reach consensus on a single diagnostic terminology/classification system for thyroid FNA interpretations, but did agree to a set of cytomorphologic features for each of the major categories of benign and malignant thyroid FNA diagnoses, which are summarized in Table 3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conference was successful in providing a framework for the development of an evidence based classification scheme for thyroid cytopathology.
the NCI FNA State of the Science meeting was a great success.

the NCI FNA State of the Science meeting has provided a consensus classification scheme for thyroid FNAS and a comprehensive set of cytomorphologic diagnostic criteria for the interpretation of thyroid FNAS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thyroid FNA diagnosis of a neoplasm is a diagnosis of a neoplastic lesion.
we can use the same criteria for cytologic interpretation of thyroid FNA that we use for the histologic interpretation of surgical thyroid specimens.
we can use the data we have to improve the accuracy of diagnosis of thyroid nodules, and thereby reduce the number of unnecessary thyroidectomies.
